content.overview: BNS s. 65 — Punishment for rape in certain cases.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Rape of a woman under 16: minimum 20 years to life for the remainder of natural life. Under 12: 20-to-life or death. Age bands are a favourite exam trap. BNS restatement of IPC 376(3), 376AB. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 65 is the rule on “Punishment for rape in certain cases”. The section provides that (1) Whoever, commits rape on a woman under sixteen years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, and shall also be liable to fine:. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 65 exists so that “Punishment for rape in certain cases” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
65. (1) Whoever, commits rape on a woman under sixteen years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, and shall also be liable to fine:

(2) Whoever, commits rape on a woman under twelve years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, and with fine or with death:

Essential ingredients
1. (1) Whoever, commits rape on a woman under sixteen years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, and shall also be liable to fine:
2. (2) Whoever, commits rape on a woman under twelve years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, and with fine or with death:

Punishment / legal consequence
Under 16: 20-to-life (remainder). Under 12: 20-to-life or death.

Exceptions, limitations and provisos
Sub-section (1): the fine must be just and reasonable to meet the victim’s medical expenses and rehabilitation; any fine imposed under this sub-section must be paid to the victim.

Sub-section (2): the same fine-related requirements apply separately under this sub-section; any fine imposed under this sub-section must be paid to the victim.

sections.heading: The legal rule
sections.body:
65. (1) Whoever, commits rape on a woman under sixteen years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, and shall also be liable to fine:

hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 65 (Punishment for rape in certain cases), Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever commits rape on a woman under sixteen years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, and shall also be liable to fine:
   (2) Whoever commits rape on a woman under twelve years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, and with fine or with death:
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 65 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 65 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

learningObjectives: Understand the child rape sentencing provisions under BNS s. 65.
Analyze subsection (1): rape of girl under sixteen years (minimum 20 years to natural life).
Analyze subsection (2): rape of girl under twelve years (minimum 20 years to natural life, or death).
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 65 provides enhanced punishments for rape of minor girls: (1) Whoever commits rape on a woman under sixteen years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life, and shall also be liable to fine; (2) Whoever commits rape on a woman under twelve years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life, or with death, and shall also be liable to fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: The sexual violation of children and young adolescents represents an extreme assault on human innocence, justifying statutory minimum terms of twenty years, natural-life imprisonment, and capital punishment for child victims under twelve years.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 65 (corresponding to IPC ss. 376AB and 376DA/DB frameworks).
Subsection (1): Victim under 16 years — RI minimum 20 years, extending to natural life + fine.
Subsection (2): Victim under 12 years — RI minimum 20 years, extending to natural life, OR DEATH + fine.
Victim relief: Fine shall be just and reasonable to meet medical and rehabilitation costs.
essentialIngredients: Rape was committed on a female under sixteen years (subsection 1), OR on a female under twelve years (subsection 2).
Age of victim established through birth records, matriculation certificate, or ossification test.
Penalty: Minimum 20 years RI extending to natural life (sub-sec 1); minimum 20 years, natural life, or death (sub-sec 2).
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 65 reflects the nation's zero-tolerance policy towards child sexual abuse. It bifurcates child victims into two age groups. For victims under sixteen, the statutory minimum is twenty years of rigorous imprisonment extending to natural life. For victims under twelve years, the legislature introduces capital punishment as an alternative sentencing option alongside natural-life imprisonment. The section operates concurrently with the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.
examples: Teaching example (Rape of fourteen-year-old): An accused commits rape on a fourteen-year-old student. Section 65(1) applies; the court must award a minimum sentence of twenty years rigorous imprisonment extending to natural life.
Teaching example (Rape of ten-year-old): An accused commits rape on a ten-year-old child. Section 65(2) is attracted; the court has jurisdiction to award death penalty or natural life imprisonment.
distinctions: Section 64 vs Section 65: Section 64 has a 10-year minimum for adult victims; Section 65 establishes a 20-year minimum for girls under sixteen/twelve.
Under 16 (s. 65(1)) vs Under 12 (s. 65(2)): Under 16 carries life; Under 12 introduces the death penalty.
problemApplication: Issue: What is the sentencing exposure of an accused convicted of rape of an eleven-year-old girl?
Rule: Under BNS s. 65(2), rape of a female under twelve years carries a minimum of twenty years RI, extending to natural life, or death.
Application: The victim's age is established as eleven years by official birth certificate.
Conclusion: The accused faces a minimum of 20 years RI, up to natural life, or capital punishment.
